root_cause: An own image row has a random temporary id until its upload finishes (DM ContactChat.sendImageMessage and the group image send in ChatStoreContext), but it offered the same message actions and reactions as a sent message. A delete or reaction then targeted an id no peer ever sees, and the final row under the real id came back untombstoned (and without the reaction) once the upload finished.
fix: ChatMessage.uploading (true only on the optimistic image row; the final row sets it undefined, so no stored row has it true). canShowMessageActions hides delete/edit for it; the new canReactToMessage gates ChatBox's reaction picker, long-press and badge row; the DM and group delete, edit and reaction handlers return early for an uploading row (covering the e2e bridges too).

tests_added.kinds: canShowMessageActions / canReactToMessage for uploading rows; behavioural group delete+edit refusal (no send, view unchanged); pendingOwnSends round trip (remounted view keeps the flag, final row drops it); source scans of both image sends, the DM handlers, the ChatBox reaction gates and both reaction handlers. (The round-1 reaction tests were written with the remediation, not before it.)

mutation.survivors: 1 pre-existing, outside this change: latest-message tie-break `>` vs `>=` at messageActionUi.ts:184 (equal createdAt).

e2e.result: non-relay 72 passed; relay 353 passed, 0 failed, 19 skipped; no INVALID marker.

retrospective.harder_than_needed: Message-level affordances are gated in two independent places in ChatBox (canShowMessageActions for edit/delete, bare onReact for reactions); the first fix covered only one, which both reviewers caught.
retrospective.surprised_by: The group image send had the same temporary-id defect as the DM one, though the finding named only DMs.
